label: Zero-dimensional base
title: Does one law-to-state selector recur across the first two dimensional rungs?
summary: An exact local audit compares 0D→1D and 1D→2D shell selectors after exposing unavoidable address/program role overlap. The same multiplexer semantics survives, while the Z1 patch requires exactly two dual-role cells and the frozen Gray geometry realizes no nontrivial familiar ECA symmetry.
takeaway: The bottom two shell constructions share one local selector semantics, but their physical role accounting changes from disjoint to necessarily overlapping; this is a local architecture result, not a dynamical or intrinsic-dimension theorem.
